ranked.headline: Graph and transformer models link single-cell multi-omics to regulatory structure
ranked.summary: Paired single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin profiles now feed graph and foundation models that infer enhancer-gene links and perturbation responses.

ranked.headline: Protein language models adapted to dynamics, function, and low-data prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers adapt ESM-2 and related pLM embeddings with latent, contrastive, and structural objectives for specific prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Graph learning maps tissue domains and cell states in spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: Spatial omics methods now jointly model histology, expression, and cell-cell communication to resolve tissue organization at single-cell resolution.

ranked.headline: Computational models link tumor single-cell and bulk profiles to outcome and therapy
ranked.summary: Single-cell and multi-omics tools increasingly predict survival, drug response and microenvironment organization from co-assayed profiles.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based deep learning predicts splicing, TF binding, and protein modifications
ranked.summary: Multi-species benchmarking now quantifies 21–33% AUROC losses for task-specific and foundation genomic models, sharpening scrutiny of generalization.

ranked.headline: Generative models design proteins and binders with atomic detail and diversity objectives
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend biomolecular generators to fully atomic co-design, Pareto objectives, and set-level diversity rewards.

ranked.headline: Graph-based deep learning models predict drug, protein, and metabolite interactions
ranked.summary: Attention-based graph models with multimodal fusion and explicit structural terms are now applied across drug, protein, and RNA prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Context-aware models extend regulatory variant mapping to tandem repeats and pleiotropy
ranked.summary: Context-resolved models now assign regulatory effects across tissues, cohorts, tandem repeats and disease subtypes.

ranked.headline: ML on histology and omics data predicts cancer biomarkers and treatment response
ranked.summary: Multi-omics and histology-based deep learning methods are being benchmarked and validated against clinical outcomes for cancer biomarker discovery.

ranked.headline: Precision, stochastic noise, and differentiable models reshape biological simulation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair stochastic formulations with reduced-precision arithmetic and differentiable simulators for inference over biological models.

ranked.headline: Foundation models and label-free readouts for quantitative biomedical imaging
ranked.summary: Foundation-model segmentation is now benchmarked against human-grade references across organoids, microtubules, and spatial omics imaging.

ranked.headline: Learned protein priors guide sequence design, now tested against simple baselines
ranked.summary: Recent work couples protein language model priors with epistatic and specificity models, while benchmarks question pLM gains on dense landscapes.

ranked.headline: Joint taxonomic-functional and DNA language model embeddings for microbiome analysis
ranked.summary: Fusing DNA language model embeddings with taxonomic and functional metagenomic profiles now targets binning, disease classification, and phenotype discovery.

ranked.headline: Coupled Binding and Folding of NS2B/NS3 Protease and Linker Effects Revealed by Topology-based Modeling
ranked.summary: Coarse-grained Go-model simulations map WNV NS2B/NS3 protease binding and folding; G4SG4 linker alters folding, destabilizes NS2B C-term.

ranked.headline: Split design decides whether larger molecular models beat classical predictors
ranked.summary: Benchmarks across random, scaffold and cluster splits test whether predictive gains from scale hold when test molecules depart from training data.

ranked.headline: Learned alignment methods integrate heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics data
ranked.summary: Recent methods address mosaic, weakly linked, and privacy-constrained single-cell data by learning shared representations across modalities and batches.

ranked.headline: Quality-control frameworks for reproducible genome mining and metagenomic analysis
ranked.summary: Recent tools and evaluations target error control, contamination detection, and benchmark validity in genome mining and metagenomic workflows.

ranked.headline: GNNs over biological knowledge graphs, structures, and genomic context for prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply graph architectures to multi-omics, PPI, operon, and ortholog tasks, with new signed, distance-aware, and cross-species designs.

ranked.headline: Per-site polyadenylation inference from single-cell RNA-seq is benchmarked and extended
ranked.summary: Systematic benchmarks and new deep learning and differential testing tools now address polyadenylation site inference at single-site resolution.

ranked.headline: Learned models pair TCR, peptide and HLA features for immune recognition prediction
ranked.summary: Recent items pair structure benchmarks, deep epitope predictors and cytokine-context models for TCR and peptide recognition.

ranked.headline: Annotated resources and 3D mapping sharpen protein function inference
ranked.summary: Annotated yeast interactome, phosphosite, and variant-to-structure resources now supply AI-ready inputs for function inference.

ranked.headline: Long-read and single-cell tools resolve haplotypes, structural variants and copy number
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell sequencing now support haplotype-resolved and copy-number-level inference across human genomes and cancer samples.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools for reproducible omics and biochemical network analysis
ranked.summary: Demand for reproducible, scalable analysis of network-structured metabolic and omics data is driving newly released open-source packages.

ranked.headline: Genomic prediction methods, from heuristics to deep learning, under benchmark review
ranked.summary: Reviews and commentary now stress comparative benchmarking, open datasets, and reproducibility for computational genomics predictions.

ranked.headline: AI and computational methods predict and design aptamer, RNA and Cas9 systems
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and design tools assess AI structure predictors and computational design for aptamer, RNA and Cas9 systems.

ranked.headline: Agent-mediated querying coupled to interactive viewers for spatial omics analysis
ranked.summary: Spatial omics tools are moving toward session-persistent agentic systems that keep analysis tied to direct tissue visualization.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale assemblies resolve polyploid haplotypes and pangenome variation
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved polyploid assemblies and population-scale pangenomes now link structural variation to trait mapping and recombination analysis.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking RNA-seq pipelines, nanopore modification calls, single-cell transcriptomics
ranked.summary: Pipeline choices for RNA-seq and nanopore data are now being tested against orthogonal qRT-PCR and experimental ground-truth references.

ranked.headline: Machine learning refines cryo-EM segmentation and particle picking with few labels
ranked.summary: Few-shot SAM2 picking needing five labeled micrographs and AlphaFold-informed Phenix segmentation now appear together in recent cryo-EM work.

ranked.headline: Mass spectrometry analysis tools are judged on sensitivity, cost, and evaluation rigor
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report measured gains in low-input DIA, search-engine cost, and PTM detection, alongside explicit performance benchmarking.

ranked.headline: Explicit generative and inference layers determine protein and RNA model estimates
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published VIRSE study model sequence design, ancestral reconstruction, and RNA ensemble inference explicitly.

ranked.headline: Interactive tools for exploring protein, pangenome, and assembly graph data
ranked.summary: Large protein, pangenome, and assembly datasets increasingly require lightweight browser and CLI tools for direct inspection and analysis.

ranked.headline: Mass spectrometry peptides mapped to exons, smORFs, and non-canonical genomic origins
ranked.summary: Peptide-level identification now resolves exon junctions, small ORFs, and shared peptides with explicit statistical error control.

ranked.headline: Reference-free pipelines are benchmarked for detecting spreading viruses in metagenomes
ranked.summary: Preprints benchmark reference-independent viral detection and release an end-to-end longitudinal variant tracker for pathogen variant analysis.

ranked.headline: Parameterized shape and vertex models link morphology to mechanics and flow
ranked.summary: Recent preprints invert tissue mechanics toward target shapes and couple dorsal morphology to hydrodynamics with reduced-order models.

ranked.headline: Computational models resolve chromatin accessibility, folding, and enhancer contacts
ranked.summary: Probabilistic, fractal, and cohesin-bridging models now quantify single-cell accessibility and 3D genome organization from snATAC-seq and Hi-C data.

ranked.headline: Diagnosing failure modes of statistical models in genomic and single-cell inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications test when GRN inference, RNA-seq normalization and omics fusion models fail under realistic data pathologies.

ranked.headline: Single-cell snapshots decoded into dynamics by velocity, barcode clocks and chromatin maps
ranked.summary: Recovering temporal dynamics from single-cell snapshots requires mechanistic models that integrate spatial, chromatin, and lineage-barcode information.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic ODE models link receptor trafficking and avidity to cellular response
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend mechanistic models to endosomal recycling, multivalent avidity and pathway model selection at receptor level.

ranked.headline: Genetic architecture and spatial structure shape selection outcomes in mechanistic models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study link epistasis, spatial structure, and dosage response to selection outcomes and trait buffering.
